description: Diagnosis-first data-layer fix. FIRST write failing reproduction tests proving: cross-user node-status leak (status is stamped on globally shared nodes while the user->item edge is per user; already reproduced in a scratch run: node needsReview vs edge approved), stale baked status in useAccessMatrix, missing/spurious first hop (zero-composition AP/role, blank labels), aggregation order-dependence, id-space matching. THEN fix every confirmed cause: review status becomes a LIVE per-user overlay (domain/reviewOverlay.ts) keyed by reviewKey(userId,kind,accessId|name) applied to structural first-level edges; remove baked reviewStatus from rows; derive node status from the user's first-level edge inside userSubgraph; one aggregation rule (needsReview > reassigned > revoked > approved) in domain/metrics.ts with a mixed flag; wire the overlay into useAccessMatrix via useMemo so resolution is not re-run on a decision. FEAT-002 depends on this FEAT.

Shared fixture from plan.md: user A holds AP ap-bill{e-pay}, role role-a{AP ap-foo{e-read,e-write}, ent e-del}, direct e-login (approved), e-admin (revoked), e-read held directly AND nested in ap-foo; user B holds e-login (needsReview) and ap-bill (reassigned). Run `npx vitest run src/domain src/graph src/state src/sailpoint` and RECORD the failing test names in this file's `findings` (tests that unexpectedly pass are guards; note them). If a test needs a not-yet-existing export, add a minimal stub signature so failures are assertion failures, not import errors.

If the AP resolves with zero entitlementRefs, or the role resolves with zero AP refs and zero entitlement refs, return ONE bare first-level row (name/id of the item, blank entitlement/source, unresolved:false) instead of []. When row.accessItemKind is set, ensure the matching level is present (if its label is blank use row.accessItemName, then 'Unnamed <kind>', id from accessItemId) so the first hop is never replaced by a deeper node. Set edge.firstLevel=true and edge.reviewKey=reviewKey(row.userId,row.accessItemKind,row.accessItemId,row.accessItemName) on the user->levels[1] edge only when levels[1].kind === row.accessItemKind; otherwise create the edge without the marker. Confirm the repro tests now PASS; run `npx tsc -b` and fix consumers of the removed row.reviewStatus (grep src for row-level `.reviewStatus`) without touching accessCounts.ts or CampaignDashboard*. AccessGraphCanvas.tsx/AccessMatrixView.tsx need no change here beyond compiling; buildAccessScene/AccessNode keep compiling with node.reviewStatus now sourced from userSubgraph. Update any existing graph test fixtures that relied on rows carrying reviewStatus (buildAccessScene.test.ts, AccessGraphCanvas.test.tsx, AccessMatrixView.test.tsx) minimally by building them through applyReviewStatus + userSubgraph so the suite compiles and passes; FEAT-002 then adds the new reference assertions.

Commit locally on the branch: `fix: per-user live review-status overlay for drill-down graph` with the gate results and the list of reproduction tests that failed before the fix in the message. Never push.
acceptance_criteria: Before any source edit the reproduction tests named in the steps were run and the failing ones are listed in findings.
For two users sharing an entitlement with different statuses, userSubgraph for each user shows node status equal to that user's own user->node edge status, and a nested-only node has no status.

Changing a review item's decision after resolution changes the graph's first-level edge status via useAccessMatrix with no additional getRoleV1/getAccessProfileV1/getEntitlementV1 call, and graph.nodes keeps the same array reference.
The set of edges with firstLevel===true from a user node equals exactly the set of that user's non-'access' review items (including empty AP/role and blank-label cases).
Aggregation is deterministic regardless of item order and flags mixed; REVIEW_STATUS_RANK exists in exactly one place.
AccessMatrixRowVM has no reviewStatus; rowKey unchanged; accessCounts.test.ts and CampaignDashboard tests pass unmodified.
`npm run build`, `npm run lint`, `npm test` pass.

findings:
FAILING BEFORE (14, against unchanged source; domain/reviewOverlay.ts was a no-op stub so they fail on assertions):
- useAccessMatrix > reflects a decision made after resolution in graph edge status without re-resolving (edge stayed needsReview: Cause B confirmed)
- userSubgraph review status > stamps node status only from this user's first-level edge (no cross-user leak) (needsReview vs approved: Cause A confirmed)
- userSubgraph review status > a nested-only node carries no status in another user's drill-down (nested e-write showed 'approved': confirmed)
- userSubgraph review status > node status always equals its incoming user edge status across a mixed fixture (confirmed)
- deriveAccessGraph first-level structure > user->X edges equal exactly the user's review items (no firstLevel marker; zero-composition AP and blank-named role first hops missing/replaced: confirmed)
- deriveAccessGraph first-level structure > never stamps a review status on a node during derivation (old derivation stamped nodes)
- resolveMatrix > emits a first-level row for an access profile with zero entitlements (old: []) ; > emits a first-level row for a role with no access profiles or entitlements (old: [])
- reviewOverlay > matches by the review item's own accessId even when the resolved composition id differs; > falls back to the access name when accessId is null; > aggregates several review items ... independent of order; > flags mixed statuses; > skips 'access'-kind items and keeps users apart; > applyReviewStatus does not mutate its input and reuses the nodes array (all fail on the stub: no firstLevel/reviewKey/reviewMixed existed).
GUARDS (passed before and after): 'deriveAccessGraph > deeper edges never carry a review status or first-level marker' (deeper edges were never stamped: not a bug); old derivation already created exactly one user->levels[1] edge per held item, so the spurious-first-hop concern was only the blank-label/zero-composition cases, not extra edges. ID-space mismatch and null accessId were NOT live bugs in old code (row-baked status matched by construction); they are now guarded by matching on the review item's own accessId/accessName on both sides.
CONFIRMED CAUSES FIXED: A (global node status leak), B (stale baked status in useAccessMatrix), C (no structural first-level marker), zero-composition AP/role vanishing, blank-label first hop replaced by deeper node, duplicate rank tables. Aggregation order-dependence was not a live bug (rank-based merge was order independent) but is now one rule with a mixed flag.
